item.title: Former U.S. Marine held in Russia on disputed charges has been released
item.description: Russia released an American military veteran, allowing his return to the U.S. after four years of what his family and U.S. officials allege was wrongful incarceration and abusive treatment.

item.title: Earthquake response strains Colombia's new government and rescuers
item.description: The earthquake killed at least 181 people and left 2,595 injured, according to Colombian authorities. At least 195 remained missing, but civilian-run databases put that number closer to 4,000.
item.content:encoded:
The earthquake killed at least 181 people and left 2,595 injured, according to Colombian authorities. At least 195 remained missing, but civilian-run databases put that number closer to 4,000.

(Image credit: Ivan Valencia)

item.title: Progressive Peggy Flanagan wins Democratic Senate primary in Minnesota
item.description: Progressive Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan won the Democratic primary for Senate from Minnesota. It continues a series of wins for the progressive wing of the party over centrists.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Trump-backed Mike Lindell loses primary for Minnesota governor to Lisa Demuth
item.description: Lindell had President Trump's endorsement but he lost to Lisa Demuth, the speaker of the state house. She'll face Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar in the fall for governor.

item.title: In South Carolina, Sen. Darline Graham advances to a GOP special primary runoff for U.S. Senate
item.description: Sen. Darline Graham, who is serving out the remainder of her brother's term, and Rep. Ralph Norman advance to the special primary runoff later this month.

item.title: The death toll climbs from Monday's 7.4 magnitude earthquake in Colombia
item.description: Hundreds of rescue workers have been deployed in hardest hit cities trying to free victims still trapped under the rubble. Hundreds of people are still missing.

item.title: A judge expands a block on U.S. Postal Service work on Trump's mail-in voting order
item.description: A federal judge expanded a block on a key part of President Trump's order to restrict mail-in voting for this fall's midterms, banning the Postal Service from carrying out directives in every state.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Kennedy Center must pay $250,000 in legal fees to musician who canceled in protest
item.description: Chuck Redd canceled his annual Christmas Eve performance to protest Trump's name being added to the complex. In June, a superior court judge dismissed the Kennedy Center's lawsuit against Redd.
